reread_from_the_machine.doctor: channel nightly (from the Homebrew formula lisa-nightly), installed 0.5.0, level; one lisa at /opt/homebrew/bin/lisa and `lisa` runs it; zellij 0.44.3 system, supported
reread_from_the_machine.read_it_with_the_job's_PATH: PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, the same one the launch agent sets. A plain non-login ssh has none of Homebrew on PATH, and doctor run that way reports `lisa install unsupported` and `zellij unsupported` about a machine that is fine. Set the PATH or you will read a healthy box as broken.
reread_from_the_machine.guard_seen_live: a live zellij session (`overseer`, running `claude --continue`) was up during this read, so tonight's 04:37 run will log `held` rather than move

not_yet_true: Rollback has not been performed on this machine. It was rehearsed on the dev desk; `lisa upgrade --tag` on a Homebrew box leaves a second lisa in ~/.local/bin and that path is untested here. It needs the mini idle — the renderer loop was live all evening and swapping the binary under it is the exact failure the held guard exists to prevent.
data.why_this_machine: It runs real work. renderer had 35 done and a live loop when this was written. A nightly box with nothing on it proves nothing and reports healthy while doing so.

alert.leaves_the_box: A failed night writes ~/ergo-fleet/lisa-stay-current.alert on the mini — schema lisa.nightly-alert/v1, carrying the host, the formula, why it failed, whether any lisa is still installed, whether `lisa --version` still answers, and brew's own words. The laptop reads it over the reach desk.toml already spells (`ssh mini cat ~/ergo-fleet/lisa-stay-current.alert`). A success deletes the file, so a file sitting there always means the LAST attempt failed, not that one once did.
alert.how_it_used_to_lie: brew upgrade's exit status was thrown away and the outcome was inferred from comparing the version before and after, so a failed upgrade logged `current at 0.5.0 on lisa-nightly` — the same words a healthy no-op prints. The status is now kept and there are four outcomes, each one word at the front of the line: held / current / moved / failed.
alert.also_covered: brew update failing is its own failure now. Without it, `current` would be a claim about a shelf the machine never managed to look at.

proved_it_shouts.how: A sandboxed copy of the real script — three edits only: a formula that cannot exist, temp log/alert paths, and the live-session guard raised so the rest of the script was reachable while renderer was looping. No package on this machine was touched.
proved_it_shouts.logged: failed — brew upgrade lisa-no-such-formula-20260814 exited 1 and NO lisa-no-such-formula-20260814 is installed
proved_it_shouts.alert_said: why=brew upgrade exited 1, lisa_still_runs=lisa 0.5.0 — so a reader learns the box is not dead in the same breath as learning the night failed
proved_it_shouts.and_the_good_night: The same copy with brew stubbed to succeed deleted the alert file and logged `current at`, exit 0. Both directions verified.

alert.why_a_pull_and_not_a_push: The desk's rule is no-background: nothing on the mini opens a port, waits, or pushes to a third-party service the operator did not choose. Which off-box channel — a webhook, a push service, mail — is the operator's call and is asked in the 2026-08-14 night brief. screen-design T-025-03 is the ticket for making a fact filed on one machine reach the desk properly.
